topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I can't shake the chill in my bones, not a cold one, but a settling deep down. I walked the path to the village, the one we used to run, laughing, under the shadow of the old oak. It's as if the sky's grown heavier, pressing down on me. My friend, from the days when the world was just this valley, doesn't remember. I spoke his name, brought up the times we spent chasing rabbits or helping with the harvest, but the light in his eyes didn’t change. It’s as if the soil of my memory is barren, and what’s planted there has withered. The saints be with me, I whisper, for the road ahead looks long and unfamiliar.
